pdm-pulmonary-imaging: Which rib does the sternal angle mark?
The second rib
Which intercostal space does the nipple line mark?
The fifth intercostal space
Which lobes lie below the base of the fifth rib?
The inferior lobes
What lies deep to the jugular notch?
The trachea
Between which vertebral levels is the larynx?
C3 to C6
What two structures does the posterior triangle of the neck contain?
The subclavian vein and the lung apices
What does the carotid triangle contain?
The bifurcation of the common carotid artery
Which muscle divides the anterior and posterior triangles of the neck?
The sternocleidomastoid
What is the most common radiologic study?
The chest radiograph
What share of radiology images ordered in the United States are radiographs?
Which two chief complaints are most associated with chest radiographs?
Pain and shortness of breath
Which chest film view is taken supine and magnifies the heart?
Anteroposterior
Which chest film view is taken with the patient ambulatory?
Posteroanterior
What is the rounded bulge at the top of the left mediastinal border?
The aortic knob (aortic arch)
What should the costophrenic angles look like on a normal film?
Sharp Vs
What is the dark bubble under the left hemidiaphragm?
The gastric bubble (gas in the stomach)
What is the most a normal heart may span on a posteroanterior film?
Half of the chest
How does the one-third, two-thirds rule split the heart?
One third right of the midline, two thirds left
Which hilum is normally slightly higher?
The left
What makes up most of each hilum?
The pulmonary arteries and veins
Where should the trachea sit on a chest film?
In the midline
Which vessels should be the only real vascular markings on a chest film?
The pulmonary arteries and veins
How are the ribs assessed on a chest film?
One at a time, both sides, then the next one down
Which two spaces are assessed after the lung fields?
The retrosternal and retrocardiac spaces
What shape does the normal thoracic spine have on a lateral chest film?
A posterior arch
Which sinuses is the Water's view for?
The maxillary and frontal sinuses
At what angle to the orbitomeatal line is the Water's view taken?
45 degrees
Which space on the lateral neck film holds the esophagus?
The retrotracheal space
What does an airless esophagus on a lateral neck film mean?
Normal: it is collapsed when not eating
What partly obscures the vertebral body below C7 on a lateral neck film?
The first rib
What curve should the cervical spine show?
A slight anterior curve (lordosis)
How does an overexposed chest film look?
Dark, with the spine and retrocardiac areas showing
How does an underexposed chest film look?
White, with no spine or mediastinal anatomy
Which exposure lets you trace a nasogastric tube behind the heart?
Overexposure
To which posterior rib should the diaphragm domes reach on a standing inspiration?
The tenth
How is rotation assessed on a frontal film?
Spinous processes to the clavicle borders
What should never be used to judge rotation?
The tracheal shadow
What is the pleura checked for on the radiographic anatomy checklist?
Effusion, thickening, calcification
What are the hila checked for on the checklist?
Masses and lymphadenopathy
What soft-tissue finding should never be missed on a chest film?
A mastectomy
When does computed tomography come before the chest radiograph?
Only for suspected pulmonary embolism (angiogram)
Past what duration is an unexplained cough an indication for a chest radiograph?
6 weeks
What is the most common reason to order chest computed tomography?
An inconclusive radiograph with a continuing problem
Which modality is best for bone?
Computed tomography
What are the true contraindications to radiographs?
None
What test is always ordered before imaging a female of childbearing age?
A beta human chorionic gonadotropin (pregnancy) test
Is pregnancy an absolute contraindication to imaging?
No; emergent studies are done, even with contrast
What is pulmonary ultrasound used for, almost exclusively?
Trauma: a collapsed lung or fluid
What are the contraindications to pulmonary ultrasound?
None
What do high and low attenuation mean on computed tomography?
Bright and dark
What attenuation is fresh blood from a hemorrhage?
High (bright)
Which allergy history, untested for iodine, is a contrast caution?
Anaphylaxis to shellfish
Why is a high creatinine a contrast caution?
Contrast is renally cleared and nephrotoxic
Where is the descending aorta on a transverse angiogram?
Left of the patient's vertebral column
Which ventricle lies closest to the sternal wall?
The right ventricle
When is a ventilation/perfusion scan used?
Pulmonary embolism when the angiogram can't be done (contrast allergy)
How does the ventilation/perfusion scan compare with the angiogram?
It is inferior
How is the ventilation/perfusion result reported?
Low, medium or high probability
What is positron emission tomography mostly used for?
Finding metastases
For which aortic problem is magnetic resonance superior to the angiogram?
Intramural hematoma
Which metal implants are not a magnetic resonance precaution?
Titanium
What does pneumonia look like on a chest film?
Consolidation
What is the radiograph sign of a pleural effusion?
Blunted costophrenic angles
What causes Kerley B lines?
Thickened interlobular septa
Which four film signs make up pulmonary edema?
Cephalization, Kerley B lines, effusion, larger cardiothoracic ratio
How does a pneumothorax look on a chest film?
Jet black, with the compressed lung beside it
Which part of the lung does interstitial lung disease affect?
The interstitium, not the air sacs
What are clustered ring-like cystic spaces of 3 to 10 millimeters called?
Honeycombing
What are hazy, pale areas of increased lung density called?
Ground-glass opacities
